name: device_bridge
title: How a phone connection crosses the device bridge
summary: TCP packets enter the VPN interface, are rewritten back to the host kernel, and become one destination stream OPEN through libyume. Replies reverse the same path.

nodes.title: Phone application
nodes.note: The application asks its own kernel to connect to a destination. Its packets enter the VPN interface.

nodes.title: VPN interface
nodes.note: The embedding app owns the TUN descriptor, addresses and routes. Android supplies it through VpnService.

nodes.title: Rewrite and reinject
nodes.note: DeviceNat remembers the destination, rewrites addresses and ports, updates checksums and sends the segment back into the device.

nodes.title: Host TCP listener
nodes.note: The host kernel terminates TCP at the bridge listener. The listener rejects connections the translator did not create.

nodes.title: libyume stream OPEN
nodes.note: The bridge joins the local socket to one authenticated stream OPEN on the kit's TCP service. UDP uses packet OPENs instead.

nodes.title: yumed
nodes.note: The ordinary server checks the identity grant and destination policy before opening a socket. It needs no phone-specific service.

nodes.title: Destination
nodes.note: The destination gets a connection from the server. Application HTTPS, when used, still ends at the destination.
